documents.title: Varenholt Observatory
documents.text:
Title: Varenholt Observatory

The Varenholt Observatory sits on the ridge above the town of Kestrel Hollow. It was founded in 1987 by the astronomer Ilse Marrow, who raised the funds through a public subscription. Its primary instrument is the Aldous Reflector, a 2.4 metre telescope. The observatory opens to the public on clear Friday nights and runs a schools programme every spring.

documents.title: Brindlewick Ferry Company
documents.text:
Title: Brindlewick Ferry Company

The Brindlewick Ferry Company operates the Tamsin route across Lake Orrin, linking Kestrel Hollow with the eastern shore villages. Its flagship vessel is the Quiet Heron, a forty metre catamaran. The company was founded by Rowan Petch, a former fisherman, and still keeps its ticket office on the old stone quay.

documents.title: Solenne Bakery
documents.text:
Title: Solenne Bakery

The Solenne Bakery opened on Pewter Street in 2003 and is run by Maribel Quist. It is famous for the Larkloaf, a cardamom rye bread that sells out most mornings before nine. The bakery supplies bread to the Hollow Gazette staff canteen and to the Saturday market stalls.

documents.title: Kestrel Hollow Town Council
documents.text:
Title: Kestrel Hollow Town Council

The Kestrel Hollow Town Council meets on the first Tuesday of every month in Tolliver Hall. The current mayor is Oskar Lindqvist-Vale, elected in 2022. The town has a population of 14,200 residents according to the latest census, and the council employs a staff of thirty-eight.

documents.title: Project Halcyon
documents.text:
Title: Project Halcyon

Project Halcyon is a battery research programme at the Dunmere Institute, led by Dr. Priya Vantongeren. The team develops sodium-graphite anodes and targets an energy density of 400 watt-hours per kilogram. The programme began in 2020 with a grant from the regional energy board and employs fourteen researchers.

documents.title: Dunmere Institute
documents.text:
Title: Dunmere Institute

The Dunmere Institute was founded in 1952 as a materials science laboratory. Its campus is located in Wexcombe, twelve kilometres north of Kestrel Hollow. The institute is directed by Dr. Anselm Faraday-Roux and hosts about two hundred staff across six research groups, including the Halcyon battery programme.

documents.title: Orrin Lake Regatta
documents.text:
Title: Orrin Lake Regatta

The Orrin Lake Regatta is held every August on Lake Orrin. The course record is held by Thessaly Brandt, who sailed the boat Marigold Nine to victory in 2019 in a time of two hours and eleven minutes. Around sixty boats enter each year and the finish line is beside the ferry quay.

documents.title: Copperline Railway
documents.text:
Title: Copperline Railway

The Copperline Railway is a narrow gauge line running 41 kilometres from Kestrel Hollow to Wexcombe. It opened in 1911 to carry copper ore and now runs heritage services on weekends. Its steam locomotive, the Ember Queen, was built in 1923 and restored by volunteers in 1998.

Title: Fennimore Press

Fennimore Press publishes the Hollow Gazette, a weekly newspaper with a circulation of 6,000. The editor is Beatrix Oyelaran, who joined the paper in 2015. The press occupies a converted warehouse on the quay and also prints the programme for the Orrin Lake Regatta each summer.

documents.title: Wexcombe Glassworks

Title: Wexcombe Glassworks

The Wexcombe Glassworks produces the Seaglass Blue range of tableware, coloured with a cobalt recipe kept since 1904. The master glassblower is Tobiah Renn, who trained in the works as an apprentice at sixteen. The main furnace is nicknamed Old Wren and runs day and night from September to May.

documents.title: Kestrel Hollow Library
documents.text:
Title: Kestrel Hollow Library

The Kestrel Hollow Library opens at nine each weekday and is run by the librarian Sunniva Achebe. It holds the Petch Maritime Archive, a collection of ferry logs and charts donated by the Petch family. The reading room overlooks Lake Orrin and hosts a children's story hour on Wednesdays.

documents.title: Tamsin Bridge
documents.text:
Title: Tamsin Bridge

The Tamsin Bridge is a suspension bridge across the Tamsin narrows at the southern end of Lake Orrin. It was completed in 1968 and designed by the engineer Leopold Nkemelu. The main span measures 310 metres and the deck carries two road lanes and a footpath used by the annual Lantern Walk.

documents.title: Pewter Street Market
documents.text:
Title: Pewter Street Market

The Pewter Street Market takes place every Saturday and dates from the 1890s. The stallholder association is chaired by Wilhelmina Ostrowski, a cheesemaker who has kept a stall for twenty-six years. Around seventy stalls trade from eight until two, and the market closes only for the Lantern Walk weekend.

documents.title: Aldous Reflector
documents.text:
Title: Aldous Reflector

The Aldous Reflector is a 2.4 metre telescope whose mirror was ground by the optician Casimir Aldous over two years, finishing in 1985. It was installed at the Varenholt Observatory in 1987 and remains the largest telescope in the region. The mirror is re-aluminised every five years.

documents.title: Orrin Fisheries Cooperative

Title: Orrin Fisheries Cooperative

The Orrin Fisheries Cooperative represents twenty-three boats working Lake Orrin. It is chaired by Rafferty Duquesne, who has fished the lake for thirty years. The cooperative's whitefish quota is 180 tonnes a year, and its catch is landed at the stone quay beside the ferry office.

Title: Kestrel Hollow Lantern Walk

The Kestrel Hollow Lantern Walk is held on the second Saturday of November. Walkers gather at Tolliver Hall at dusk and follow a lit route down to the Tamsin Bridge. The event is organized by the librarian Sunniva Achebe and raises money for the library's children's programme.
